content.title: FAQ | Spectrum SportsNet
content.text: If you have an issue to report, please visit https://spectrumsportsnet.com/contact. GENERAL FAQ What is Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA? Spectrum SportsNet Spectrum SportsNet is a regional sports network that launched on October 1, 2012. Through its exclusive partnerships with the Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Sparks and the California Interscholastic Federation (CIF), the 24/7, high-definition network delivers more than 130 live events per year plus extensive team coverage and behind-the-scenes access unlike anything fans have seen before. Spectrum SportsNet LA Spectrum SportsNet LA launched on February 25, 2014 as the 24/7 high-definition regional sports network exclusively dedicated to the Los Angeles Dodgers. Spectrum SportsNet LA televises over 150 live regular season games as well as Spring Training games and comprehensive coverage. Spectrum SportsNet LA's regular season live Dodgers game telecasts feature the network's award-winning pregame show, “LeadOff LA,” and its flagship pre and postgame studio programs, “Access SportsNet: Dodgers.” What other programming do fans get on Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA? Spectrum SportsNet "Access SportsNet", the network’s signature daily studio show that encompasses pre- and post-game shows as “Access SportsNet: Lakers”. "Backstage: Lakers", a weekly documentary that chronicles the Lakers season from start to finish . "Connected With…, the network’s signature interview show that features interviews with Lakers players and coaches. "LakeShow Podcast", the network's weekly deep dive into all things Lakers hosted by Spectrum SportsNet hosts Allie Clifton, Chris McGee and Mike Bresnahan. "Lakers Top Ten"; one-hour episodes that break down the top 10 moments in Lakers history as selected by a group of former players, coaches, celebrities and media members with strong ties to the team. "Sports Shrine," a documentary series on the history, operations, and unforgettable moments of the most iconic arenas & stadiums in Los Angeles. Spectrum SportsNet LA “Access SportsNet: Dodgers,” flagship pre and postgame studio programs. “Leadoff LA,” a pregame show that features in-depth analysis and fan contributions via social media. “Backstage: Dodgers,” a weekly documentary series that chronicles the Dodgers’ season from spring training throughout the offseason. "Connected With…," an in-depth interview series. “Timeless Dodgers,” classic games. “Dodgermentary,” hour-long biographies. Where can I find more information? Spectrum SportsNet Twitter @SpectrumSN Instagram @SpectrumSportsNet Facebook www.facebook.com/SpectrumSportsNet Spectrum SportsNet LA Twitter @SportsNetLA Instagram @SportsNetLA Facebook www.facebook.com/SportsNetLA TV ACCESS Do I have to subscribe to Charter Spectrum Cable to watch these networks? No! Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA are available to some cable, satellite and telco providers. See the complete list of providers below under Where and How to Watch. What if my provider doesn’t carry Spectrum SportsNet or Spectrum SportsNet LA? Let your provider know you want Spectrum SportsNet or Spectrum SportsNet LA! Your voice is important, so make sure you let your provider know you don’t want to miss Lakers or Dodgers games and programming. Where and How to Watch Spectrum SportsNet Providers Availability AT&T U-verse Southern California (Los Angeles, San Diego, Bakersfield, and much of Fresno) with U100 Package and Above: Channel 777 – SD; Channel 1777 – HD Charter/Spectrum Channel 215 – SD Channel 787 – HD You can also visit the Spectrum Channel Lineup & Channel Guide and enter your zip code to search for Spectrum SportsNet and find the channel in your area. https://www.spectrum.com/cable-tv/channel-lineup COX Orange County & Santa Barbara: Channel 65/1065 Palos Verdes: Channel 70/1070 San Diego: Channel 71/1071 Las Vegas: Channel 66/1066 DirecTV Southern California (Los Angeles, San Diego, Bakersfield, and much of Fresno), Santa Barbara and Ventura counties, Las Vegas, and Hawaii: Channel 691 Regions: Spectrum SportsNet’s broadcast territory includes all regions that previously broadcast Lakers and Sparks games. Those areas include: California Counties: Los Angeles, Orange, Ventura, Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Riverside, San Bernadino, San Diego, Imperial, Inyo, Tulare, Fresno, Kings California Towns in Monterey County: Bradley (93426) and San Ardo (93450) Hawaii: Entire State Nevada Counties: Clark County (All Zip Codes), Esmeralda County (Zip Codes: 89010, 89013, 89047), Lincoln County (Zip Codes: 89001, 89008, 89017, 89042, 89043), and Nye County (Zip Codes: 89020, 89003, 89022, 89023, 89041, 89048, 89060, 89061, 89045, 89049) Outside Broadcast Region: If your provider carries Spectrum SportsNet outside of the area listed above, you will still be able to watch non-live game programming on the network, but not live games. All Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Sparks games that air on Spectrum SportsNet can only be watched live within the network’s local broadcast footprint, in accordance with the National Basketball Association’s (NBA) and Women’s National Broadcast Association’s (WNBA) broadcast territory rules, as was the case with the teams’ previous TV broadcast partner stations. Spectrum SportsNet LA Providers Availability AT&T TV In-Region Customers with Choice Package and Above: Channel 690 AT&T TV NOW In-Region Customers with Choice Package and Above: Channel 690 AT&T U-verse In-Region Customers with U100 Package (English) and U200 Latino Package (Spanish) and Above: Channel 780 – SD; Channel 1780 – HD Charter/Spectrum Los Angeles: Channel 44 – SD; Channel 789 – HD Porterville: Channel 44 – SD San Luis Obispo: Channel 44 – SD; Channel 773 – HD You can also visit the Spectrum Channel Lineup & Channel Guide and enter your zip code to search for Spectrum SportsNet LA and find the channel in your area. https://www.spectrum.com/cable-tv/channel-lineup Call 1-877-906-9121 to order Spectrum SportsNet LA on Spectrum DirecTV In-Region Customers with Choice Package (English) and Mas Ultra Package (Spanish) and Above: Channel 690 Regions: Spectrum SportsNet LA is available in all areas Dodgers fans could previously watch games (subject to agreements with local providers). That area stretches from Fresno County to the north to Orange County and Riverside County to the south. It also includes Hawaii and Clark County, NV. A full list of CA counties that can receive the networks is as follows: Fresno, Kern, Kings, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Tulare, Inyo and Ventura. Over-the-Air Affiliates: All Dodgers games will air exclusively on Spectrum SportsNet LA, excluding a select number of games that are selected by MLB’s national broadcast partners. We felt it was important for Dodgers fans to have an immersive, in-depth and consistent, go-to TV home for their team. Outside Broadcast Region: Spectrum SportsNet LA is available to Spectrum subscribers in the Los Angeles area and Spectrum Sports Pass customers outside of Southern California and Hawaii. In accordance with Major League Baseball’s (MLB) broadcast territory rules, live games and some other network programming will be blacked out, as was the case with the teams’ previous TV broadcast partner stations. Spanish Access: Spanish language audio is available for Dodgers game on SNLA via the Secondary Audio Programming Channel (SAP). Spectrum video customers in Los Angeles, the Desert Cities and Barstow can watch the Spanish-language game telecasts in high definition on Channel 324. LIVE STREAM ACCESS FOR SPECTRUM SPORTSNET AND SPECTRUM SPORTSNET LA Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA feature live in-market game streaming to personal computers, mobile devices and Xumo Stream Box. How many devices can watch the Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA live stream at once? If you are a Spectrum customer and connected to your Spectrum in-home WiFi, you can stream on an unlimited number of devices. If you are not a Spectrum subscriber connected to Spectrum in-home WiFi or you are streaming outside of the home, you can stream on two (2) devices concurrently. What does "Spectrum in-home WiFi" mean? How do I know if I'm in home? Spectrum in-home WiFi means you're connected to the Spectrum WiFi at the address that is on your bill. You will know if you are connected via in-home if you tap to sign into the Spectrum SportsNet app using the Spectrum provider and are not required to provide your credentials. I'm only using one device, why am I seeing stream count exceeded messaging? It is possible your account was shared with someone else who is also streaming. If you did not share your credentials, please update your password here https://www.spectrum.net/support/manage-account/spectrumnet-sign-help/. Where do I go to reset my Spectrum username or password? You can visit https://www.spectrum.net/support/manage-account/spectrumnet-sign-help/ or click "forgot username or password" in the Spectrum Sign in screen. What do I do if I receive a message saying, “We apologize, but it appears that you are currently located outside the intended coverage area” when I attempt to login to the live stream on my computer? If you are currently located inside of our coverage area, it is possible that the IP address your computer is currently using cannot be located in our database. Please follow this link to discover the IP address your computer is using. You can visit https://spectrumsportsnet.com/contact and send your current location (city, and state) and the IP address in the feedback form so we can help troubleshoot. What do I do if I receive a message saying, “Sorry, but you’re out of the serviceable area” when I attempt to login to the Spectrum SportsNet Android or iOS app? If you are currently located inside of our coverage area, please ensure that your mobile or tablet device has Location Services turned on and that you’ve allowed the Spectrum SportsNet app access to your location. Why can’t I login to view the live stream with my TV provider credentials? Try clearing your browser's cache and cookies before attempting to log in again. If that doesn't work, we recommend contacting your TV Provider to ensure that your username and password are accurate. Please find your TV Provider’s customer service number below: AT&T U-Verse: 1-800-288-2020 Catalina Broadband Solutions: 1-877-202-1491 Charter/Spectrum: 1-833-267-6094 COX: 1-800-234-3993 DirectTV: 1-800-531-5000 Hawaiian Telcom: 1-808-643-6111 SPECTRUM SPORTSNET APP The Spectrum SportsNet app is an app for iOS and Android devices, and Xumo Stream Box that allows authorized users to watch the live Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA channels as well as Spectrum SportsNet and Spectrum SportsNet LA on-demand content. What do I do if I receive a message saying, “We apologize, but it appears that you are currently located outside the intended coverage area for Spectrum SportsNet” when I attempt to watch the live stream on the SportsNet App? The ZIP Code associated with your TV Provider account is located outside of our coverage area. Why can't I use the SportsNet App while using a VPN? VPN is not supported by the Spectrum SportsNet App. Please disconnect from VPN to use the SportsNet App. Why can't I use the SportsNet App while using a proxy? Using a proxy while on the Spectrum SportsNet App is not supported. Please disconnect from the proxy to use the Spectrum SportsNet App. Why can't I mirror my device while on the SportsNet App? Mirroring devices is not supported by the Spectrum SportsNet App at this time. The app is not loading, what should I do? If the app is not loading, check your device's internet connection and try again. If the device is connected to the internet and the app still does not load, please send us a description of the issue in the feedback form on https://spectrumsportsnet.com/contact and we will investigate. If you have additional questions, comments or feedback, please fill out the feedback form to https://spectrumsportsnet.com/contact SPECTRUM SPORTSNET+ What is Spectrum SportsNet+? Spectrum SportsNet+ is a 24/7 digital stream of Spectrum SportsNet that is available to fans without a TV subscription living in the Lakers local broadcast territory. Spectrum SportsNet+ includes over 70 live Lakers games as well as pregame and postgame coverage and Emmy Award-winning original Lakers programming. What games and other content are available on Spectrum SportsNet+? 70+ local games are available for live and on-demand viewing on Spectrum SportsNet+. Lakers games exclusively broadcasted national programmers will not be available on Spectrum SportsNet+. In addition to live games, Spectrum SportsNet+ includes comprehensive pregame and postgame coverage and award-winning original programming including “Backstage: Lakers”. On demand viewing of completed Lakers games, original programming, and special coverage of historical events such as statue ceremonies and jersey retirements will also be available. Can I watch Spectrum SportsNet+ with a residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile account? Yes, in qualifying locations, 75+ live LA Lakers games are on us when you sign up for residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile services. You can stream on NBA.com or the NBA app. Where can I watch Spectrum SportsNet+? Use NBA.com or the NBA app. The NBA app is available on Xumo Stream Box, iOS, Android, PlayStation, Xbox One, Roku, Apple TV, Chromecast, Amazon Fire TV and Android TV. What if I don't have a residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile account? To become eligible for Spectrum SportsNet+, sign up for residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile services by visiting www.spectrum.com. Spectrum SportsNet+ is also available to purchase on NBA.com. To purchase, visit: www.nba.com/sportsnet. What does a Spectrum SportsNet+ subscription cost? What are the subscription options? Please visit the Spectrum SportsNet+ packages page for the most up-to-date purchase options: www.nba.com/sportsnet. Does my Spectrum SportsNet+ subscription automatically renew? Yes, monthly and annual subscriptions will automatically renew. What devices are compatible with Spectrum SportsNet+? Spectrum SportsNet+ is available exclusively on NBA.com and the NBA App. The NBA App is available across a wide range of devices. Please visit this page for a full list of supported devices. Where do I have to live to get Spectrum SportsNet+? Spectrum SportsNet+ is available to anyone who lives inside the Lakers local broadcast territory. That includes all of Southern California, Hawaii and parts of Southern Nevada. If I live outside the Lakers local broadcast territory, can I get Spectrum SportsNet+? No. You must reside within the Lakers local broadcast territory. If you reside outside the territory, local Lakers games are available via an NBA League Pass package. I already have Spectrum SportsNet via Spectrum TV, can I access Spectrum SportsNet+? Yes. Residential Spectrum TV customers who receive SportsNet as part of their service will be able to access Spectrum SportsNet+ via authentication. Current Spectrum SportsNet subscribers can also live stream games on the Spectrum SportsNet App. What happens if I am traveling? Can I still watch Spectrum SportsNet+? Yes. Spectrum SportsNet+ is available to subscribers when they travel domestically within a 30-day period. Can I share my account with friends or family? Sharing account login information is not allowed. Each account is enabled for viewing on one device only. If more than one person is logged in, the first viewer is logged out. Can I watch Lakers games in any other languages on Spectrum SportsNet+? Not at this time. Is DVR available on Spectrum Sportsnet+? No. DVR is not available on Spectrum SportsNet+. However, game replays are available approximately 3 hours after a game has completed, as well as on-demand episodes for programs like “Backstage: Lakers.” What content will be available during the offseason? Spectrum SportsNet+ offers year-round coverage of the Lakers. Off-season coverage includes new episodes of “Access SportsNet: Lakers” every week as well as comprehensive coverage of the NBA Draft, Free Agency and Summer League. In addition, Spectrum SportsNet+ offers 15+ live L.A. Sparks games. If I am having issues, where do I go? If you are experiencing technical issues, please submit a request here. SNLA+ What is SNLA+? LAKERS GAMES FOR RESIDENTIAL SPECTRUM INTERNET AND MOBILE CUSTOMERS Can I watch LA Lakers games with a residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile account? Yes, in qualifying locations, 75+ live LA Lakers games are on us when you sign up for residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile services. You can stream on NBA.com or the NBA app. How do I start watching live LA Lakers games? If you are a residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile customer in a qualifying location, you can start watching Lakers games by signing in with your Spectrum account username and password on NBA.com or in the NBA app. Where can I watch live LA Lakers games? Use NBA.com or the NBA app. The NBA app is available on Xumo Stream Box, iOS, Android, PlayStation, Xbox One, Roku, Apple TV, Chromecast, Amazon Fire TV and Android TV. You can stream on MLB.TV or the MLB app. How do I start watching live Dodgers games? If you are a residential Spectrum Internet and Mobile customer in a qualifying location, you can start watching Dodgers games by creating an account at mlb.com/dodgerstv. You'll be instructed to link your Spectrum account to your MLB.com account. Then, download the MLB app to your device(s) or go to MLB.TV and use your MLB.com username and password to enjoy 140+ live Dodgers regular season games.MLB.TV or the MLB app. Where can I watch live LA Dodgers games?
